General Motors has not changed its stance on CarPlay and Android Auto support, despite headlines to the contrary. The automaker has no plans to reintroduce phone projection features to any models that have already dropped them. Here's what's actually going on.

No, GM has not reversed its decision to abandon CarPlay

The confusion stems from an announcement last week that GM would be rolling out a new software experience for its Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra pickup trucks. The company heavily promoted a new picture-in-picture phone mirroring system that allows CarPlay and Android Auto to coexist alongside GM's own infotainment system.

Some outlets interpreted this as GM walking back its plans to ditch CarPlay, a decision it first announced back in 2023. Unfortunately, that's not the case. GM's original announcement was about dropping CarPlay support from its future EVs, and it has followed through, with the Cadillac Lyriq EV being the only exception.

GM actually never removed CarPlay or Android Auto from any of its gas-powered vehicles. So the new phone projection system in the Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra pickup trucks does not mean they've caved to pressure and restored CarPlay support in their EVs.

A GM spokesperson has confirmed this to Joanna Stern, who posted the following on X today:

The confusion is understandable. GM CEO Mary Barra said in an interview at one point that the automaker would remove CarPlay and Android Auto from gas-powered vehicles at some point. The company quickly clarified that gas-powered vehicles would continue to offer phone projection "for the foreseeable future."

In short, nothing has changed. GM has not restored CarPlay in its EVs, and its strategy remains the same. Perhaps we can interpret GM's rollout of picture-in-picture in some gas-powered vehicles as the company realizing its decision to abandon CarPlay is unpopular. But I think that's a very generous interpretation.
